analysis:
Only docs/provider/cli-reference.md changed, and no source code. The base text covers lines 1-847. The patch adds a "Local GLM qualification" section at head lines 17-60, plus a single change at head line 1716. The patch excerpt is truncated after about head line 40, and the head text and the line 1716 change were not supplied. The visible text documents these behaviours:
- The experimental GLM root loads only when DARKBLOOM_EXPERIMENTAL_GLM5_NEXT names an absolute qualification JSON file. That file pins the catalog record, manifest and aggregate hash.
- Unset, empty, `1` or malformed values, and mismatched identities, refuse GLM.
- GLM always uses native paged KV and fails closed when contiguous is requested or DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PAGED_KV is set.
- GLM serves only through embedded MTP, so mtp_mode=off or DARKBLOOM_CBV2_MTP=0 skips the model.
- The setting is not forwarded to launchd and applies to the isolated `--local` process.
- There is no target-only serving engine, and the section states that the opt-in does not qualify the model or bypass memory admission.

This is documentation only and creates no new attack surface. The visible claims fail closed, which is consistent with T-012/T-027 (weight substitution; the pinned aggregate hash is documented). The truncated text mentions the encrypted checkpoint identity, which may touch T-041 (prefix cache, encrypted SSD). Whether it describes any change to cache keys, TTL, salt scoping or the HMAC lookup could not be verified. The next pass should read the remainder of the new section and head line 1716 for claims that conflict with T-041's accepted posture. Specific points to check are the 30-minute TTL, the HMAC lookup tags, and the cacheSalt scoping.
